Definition: properly, a piercer, i.e. an arrow; by implication, a wound; figuratively, (of God) thunderbolt; the shaft of a spear
BiblicalUsage: Chets is an arrow, a piercer, and Scripture uses it for warfare, for children and for God's own judgment. The psalmist says children are as arrows in the hand of a mighty man, Elisha tells Joash to take bow and arrows and calls the arrow the Lord's deliverance, and David's song says God sent out arrows and scattered His enemies.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe children as arrows is one of the tenderest pictures in the Bible, because arrows are made to fly far. I hold that God's arrows never miss, and that is why David could sing of them in his deliverance.
